bullets.title: MU surges 22%+, crosses $1T market cap on AI/memory cycle re-rating
bullets.body: Micron shares surged 19-22% in a single session, pushing its market cap past $1 trillion alongside SK Hynix's $1T milestone. One trader highlighted a $65M bullish position that grew to $1.5B, while another noted MU May 29 $115 calls spiked 13,600% (from $0.01 to $1.36) on gamma squeeze dynamics. Options flow showed MU and NVDA with the most bullish positioning of the day.

bullets.title: NVDA commits $150B/yr to Taiwan supply chain; Rubin CPX launch in doubt
bullets.body: Jensen Huang confirmed Nvidia plans to spend up to $150B annually on Taiwan AI suppliers, reinforcing Taiwan's central role in the AI semiconductor ecosystem. Separately, an exclusive report flagged that NVIDIA's Rubin CPX inference GPU launch is now uncertain, with no confirmed memory or substrate orders placed for the H2 product.

bullets.title: AMD hits $800B market cap milestone; broad semi ATH sweep
bullets.body: AMD crossed $800B market cap for the first time ever on Tuesday. The session also saw all-time highs in AAPL, MU, AMD, MRVL, DELL, and SNDK, while semiconductors reached a record 18% weight in the S&P 500.

bullets.title: Infineon raises power semi prices twice in one quarter; Fenghua suspends orders on surge
bullets.body: Infineon, the largest power semiconductor maker, announced price hikes effective April 1 and July 1—two hikes in a single cycle—signaling strong demand momentum. Separately, China's Fenghua Advanced Technology (largest passive component maker) suspended order intake for 0402/0603 chip resistors and MLCC lines due to a surge in demand orders.

bullets.title: CCL (copper-clad laminate) supply crunch: T-glass FR4 tight, high-end bottlenecked
bullets.body: Fintwit semiconductor supply chain analyst flagged a genuine supply crunch in legacy T-glass FR4 CCL at the lagging edge, while rapid copper foil/glass fiber innovation has created a separate bottleneck at the high end. Laminate and board material prices also adjusted 10-20% higher per a separate semivision note.

bullets.title: ByteDance eyes $70B AI capex in 2026; Qualcomm wins ByteDance AI chip deal
bullets.body: ByteDance is weighing up to $70B in 2026 capex for AI infrastructure build-out. Separately, Qualcomm secured an AI data-center chip deal with ByteDance, adding a notable enterprise customer win in the AI silicon space.

bullets.title: Broadcom flagged as likely xAI/SpaceX ASIC designer; MediaTek note raises PT
bullets.body: A semiconductor analyst noted Broadcom was initially assumed to be the designer for the xAI/SpaceX ASIC. A separate MediaTek note raised the PT to NT$5,520 citing 'massive ASIC revenue likely from SpaceX project,' though MediaTek is now viewed as a potential winner.

bullets.title: S&P 500 and NASDAQ hit fresh record highs; 19th ATH of 2026 for S&P
bullets.body: Wall Street closed at fresh all-time highs on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 up 0.61% to 7,519.26 (19th ATH of 2026) and NASDAQ gaining 1.16% to 26,648.95. The rally was driven by US-Iran peace optimism and AI-linked semiconductor strength; the DOW lagged, falling 0.22%.

bullets.title: Tech ETF inflows dominant: $23B since February vs. minimal flows in other sectors
bullets.body: Tech sector ETFs have taken in $23B since February while virtually every other sector has seen minimal inflows over the same period, underscoring concentrated positioning in the AI/semiconductor complex.

bullets.title: SPX macro correlations broken: decoupled from rates, oil; tightly linked to gold
bullets.body: SPX correlations with rates and oil sit at decade lows while its correlation with gold is at decade highs and VIX correlation at 2-year highs, suggesting the US index may not be reflecting the broader macro picture.

bullets.title: S&P 500 short interest at highest since 2011; market at greed stage with crash-call crowd growing
bullets.body: Median S&P 500 short interest reached 3.0% of market cap, the highest since late 2011, even as markets trade 40% above the 2010-2019 mean. Multiple newsletters are calling for a crash but one experienced trader notes timing is the real edge, not the call itself.

bullets.title: TSLA: Cybertruck at ~10% of production target; EU market share just 0.9% vs. BYD 2.3%
bullets.body: A bearish account characterized Cybertruck as a 'commercial disaster' running at one-tenth of its production target. ACEA data showed Tesla held only 0.9% EU/UK/EFTA market share in April versus BYD's 2.3%, though Tesla's BEV share reached 4.17%. A separate WSJ report noted strong European monthly sales growth for Tesla.

bullets.title: NVDA institutional LEAPS sweep: $11.1M bet on $225 calls through 2028
bullets.body: An institutional sweep of $11.1M on NVDA $225 call LEAPS was flagged as a signal of long-term AI conviction, targeting a strike above current levels with an expiry into 2028.

bullets.title: Starlink signs 3 of 4 largest US airlines; Filtronic ($FTC) key E-band GaN supplier
bullets.body: Starlink signed three of the four largest US airlines covering 2,300+ commercial aircraft for in-flight connectivity. Filtronic supplies E-band GaN amplifiers for Starlink's RF infrastructure under a $62.5M contract signed August 2025; cumulative contracts exceed $115M and SpaceX holds warrants over 15% of Filtronic shares.

bullets.title: IREN flagged as starting new super-cycle uptrend; trader in from $52
bullets.body: A fintwit account highlighted IREN forming higher highs and higher lows, suggesting the start of a new super-cycle uptrend with expected follow-through in coming weeks. Position entry cited at $52.

bullets.title: NOK insider transaction flagged as 'extraordinary' by typically skeptical analyst
bullets.body: A tracker of officer stock transactions flagged an unusual filing at Nokia as noteworthy, describing it as 'extraordinary'—a characterization the analyst says they rarely apply to insider transactions.

bullets.title: Global DRAM revenue near $100B in Q1 2026; AI data center demand driving cycle
bullets.body: Global DRAM revenue surged to near $100B in Q1 2026, driven by AI data center demand. The analyst community flagged both long DRAM exposure and South Korea ($EWY +10% on the day) as key beneficiaries of the ongoing memory supercycle.

bullets.title: Netflix pushes back on German plan requiring greater European content investment
bullets.body: Netflix publicly hit out against a German regulatory proposal that would require streaming groups to invest more in European content production, flagging it as a potential cost headwind.

bullets.title: Meta reassigning 70% of new-grad SWEs to reinforcement learning
bullets.body: A widely-shared post noted that approximately 70% of Meta's new graduate software engineers are being reassigned to apply their skills to reinforcement learning tasks, reflecting the company's intensifying AI engineering pivot.

bullets.title: EU clears tariff cuts on US goods; USTR signals no tariff exclusion programs under Trump
bullets.body: EU governments approved legislation implementing import duty cuts on US goods as part of the EU-US trade deal. Separately, USTR Greer stated Trump is not interested in tariff exclusion programs, with Section 301 investigations to seek public comments on proposed measures.
